title: Works in preview but breaks in production
content:
## Why it happens

An app that runs flawlessly in preview can break the moment you deploy. This is almost always caused by **environmental differences** between the two runtimes — preview and production each have their own isolated environment, filesystem, and configuration.

<Info>
Preview and production are **completely separate containers**. A change in one does not automatically propagate to the other. See [Preview vs Deployed](/preview-vs-deployed-separate) for details.
</Info>

---

## Common culprits

### Environment variables not set in production

The most frequent cause. If your code reads `process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` and that variable exists in preview but not production, the app will fail.

**What to check:**

- Open the **Environment** panel in your workspace
- Confirm every variable your app needs is present in **both** Preview *and* Production columns
- Redeploy after adding missing variables

<Tip>
Agents often set variables in preview during development. You must explicitly copy or re-create them in production.
</Tip>

---

### Hardcoded `localhost` or preview URLs

Code that references `http://localhost:3000` or your preview URL (`*.preview.emergent.run`) will break in production because those addresses are unreachable from the live deployment.

**Examples:**

- API base URLs: `const API = "http://localhost:8000"`
- Webhook callbacks: `callbackUrl: "https://my-app.preview.emergent.run/hook"`
- OAuth redirect URIs hardcoded to preview

**Fix:**

Use environment variables for all URLs:

```javascript
const API_BASE = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL || "http://localhost:3000";
```

Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` differently in preview vs production.

---

### CORS configuration pointing to the wrong origin

If your backend explicitly allows only your preview domain:

```python
allowed_origins = ["https://my-app.preview.emergent.run"]
```

…production requests from `https://my-app.emergent.run` (or your custom domain) will be blocked.

**Fix:**

- Use an environment variable for allowed origins
- Or allow both domains
- Or use a wildcard pattern if security allows

---

### Files written at runtime disappear

Production containers use an **ephemeral filesystem**. Any file your app writes to disk (uploads, generated PDFs, cached images) will be lost on restart or scale-out.

**Symptoms:**

- User uploads work initially, then vanish
- Generated files return 404 after a few hours
- SQLite databases lose data

**Fix:**

Use [Emergent Object Store](/file-storage-emergent-object-store) for persistent file storage. Never rely on the local filesystem for data that must survive restarts.

<Warning title="Do not use local disk for persistence">
The container filesystem is wiped on every redeploy and can be cleared at any time during autoscaling.
</Warning>

---

### Missing system dependencies

Preview may have been running on a container that happened to have a system tool installed, but production does not.

**Common examples:**

| Tool         | Used for                           | Symptom in production                     |
|--------------|------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| `ffmpeg`     | Video encoding, audio extraction   | "ffmpeg: command not found"               |
| Playwright   | Browser automation, screenshots    | Chromium binary missing                   |
| ImageMagick  | Image resizing, format conversion  | "convert: not found"                      |
| wkhtmltopdf  | HTML-to-PDF rendering              | PDF generation fails silently             |

**Fix:**

Declare dependencies in your project:

- Add `playwright install` to your build script
- Use a Docker base image that includes the tool
- Or ask the agents to install it via system packages

If the tool was present in preview by chance, you must explicitly require it for production.

---

### Webhooks still pointing to preview

External services (Stripe, Twilio, GitHub) may still have webhook URLs pointing to your preview instance.

**What happens:**

- Payment confirmations arrive in preview but not production
- SMS replies are processed in the wrong environment
- OAuth flows redirect to the old URL

**Fix:**

- Log into each third-party service
- Update webhook/callback URLs to your production domain
- Test the flow end-to-end in production

<Tip title="Use environment-specific webhook secrets">
Store separate webhook signing secrets for preview and production so you can safely test webhooks without triggering real side effects.
</Tip>

---

## Debugging checklist

<Steps>
<Step title="Compare environment variables">
Open the Environment panel and ensure every variable in preview also exists in production with the correct value.
</Step>

<Step title="Check logs">
View production logs in the workspace. Look for missing-variable errors, connection timeouts, or "command not found."
</Step>

<Step title="Search for hardcoded URLs">
Grep your codebase for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `.preview.emergent.run` and replace with environment variables.
</Step>

<Step title="Verify CORS origins">
Ensure your backend allows requests from your production domain (or custom domain if configured).
</Step>

<Step title="Audit file writes">
If your app writes files, confirm they go to [Object Store](/file-storage-emergent-object-store), not `/tmp` or the project directory.
</Step>

<Step title="Confirm system dependencies">
If preview worked but production crashes on a missing binary, declare that dependency in your build configuration.
</Step>

<Step title="Update external webhooks">
Check every third-party integration and point webhooks to your live domain.
</Step>
</Steps>

---

## Still broken?

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="App slow or crashing" icon="gauge-high" href="/app-slow-crashing-or-cold-starting">
Performance and startup issues
</Card>
<Card title="Missing functionality" icon="wrench" href="/missing-functionality">
Feature worked in preview, now absent
</Card>
</CardGroup>

If none of the above applies, describe the exact error message in chat — agents can compare your preview and production configurations and identify the mismatch.
description: Why an app works in preview but breaks live: separate env vars, hardcoded localhost, CORS, ephemeral filesystem losing runtime files, missing system tools (ffmpeg/Playwright), webh
